questions.question: How many seats are authorized on the board or committee, how many are currently filled, and how many vacancies exist?
questions.answer: The Conservation Commission is authorized to have seven appointed members plus two liaison members (nine total). Currently, seven named appointed members are listed: Haven Colgate (Chair), Eyal Dror, Matthew Hobby, Margie Lavender, Dan Lemons, Amy Listerman, and Aarthi Muthukrishnan, plus one liaison (Trustee Fleisig). The number of vacancies is not explicitly stated, though the seven appointed seats appear filled based on the member list.

questions.question: Does the board or committee page show ongoing projects, priorities, or current work in progress?
questions.answer: The board/committee page shows ongoing projects and current work in progress. Specifically, the Hillside Woods Restoration Project (HWRP) is highlighted as a multi-year initiative focused on restoring ecological balance and habitat to Hillside Woods and Park. Ongoing work sessions are available for public participation. Current activities include removing invasive plants and replanting with native species. The Hastings Vine Squad operates seasonally (November to March) to free trees from invasive vines. A dedicated project page and the Protect Our Woods website are referenced for additional background information. Sign-up options for work sessions are provided.
questions.gap: No gap — the page clearly communicates active initiatives, current status, and ongoing work with participation opportunities and links to further project details.
